topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Project Agora - Real value testing
key_claim: Twenty-eight private sector institutions and central banks settled approximately CHF 800,000 of real value across 17 cross-border transaction scenarios on the Project Agora prototype, with an average time from payment initiation to settlement of about 80 seconds.
frame_summary: Argues that tokenisation and atomic settlement of real central bank reserves and commercial bank deposits is operationally feasible across jurisdictions and interoperable with existing RTGS and core banking systems.
cluster: Tokenised settlement moves from prototype to production
verbatim_quote: Twenty-eight private sector institutions and central banks completed transactions totalling approximately CHF 800,000 in a selection of currencies during real-value testing (RVT).
verbatim_list: Twenty-eight private sector institutions and central banks completed transactions totalling approximately CHF 800,000 in a selection of currencies during real-value testing (RVT).

Despite the prototype not being integrated with existing real-time gross settlement (RTGS) and core banking systems, the average time from payment initiation to settlement was approximately 80 seconds.
The programme covered 17 transaction scenarios, with values ranging from CHF 9,000 to CHF 125,000 or local currency equivalents.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Dollarisation and monetary control: what lessons for the rise of stablecoins?
date_evidence: meta-DC.date: 2026-07-21 ; visible on page: "BIS Working Papers | No 1370 | 21 July 2026"
key_claim: Using foreign currency deposit data and dollar-pegged stablecoin inflows for more than 130 economies, the paper finds stablecoin dollarisation shares the macro-financial drivers of deposit dollarisation but, unlike deposits, is largely unaffected by capital flow restrictions.
frame_summary: Argues that stablecoins open a new, persistent and largely capital-control-proof channel of dollarisation in emerging economies, which is a monetary-control problem rather than a banking-competition problem.
cluster: The private dollar contracts at home and spreads abroad
verbatim_quote: Drawing on data on foreign currency deposits and dollar-pegged stablecoin inflows for more than 130 economies, we compare the dynamics and drivers of "stablecoin dollarisation" with those of conventional deposit dollarisation.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: III. Anchoring trust in money: innovation beyond stablecoins (Annual Economic Report 2026)
date_evidence: meta-DC.date: 2026-06-23 ; visible on page: "BIS Annual Economic Report | 23 June 2026"
key_claim: Annual stablecoin transaction volume was an estimated 28 trillion dollars in 2025, less than three business weeks of settlement volume in the largest US wholesale payment systems, and current stablecoin designs fall short on the foundational properties of money.
frame_summary: Argues that the next monetary system should be built by integrating tokenisation into the existing two-tier architecture rather than through stablecoins, whose designs undermine the singleness and elasticity of money.
cluster: The private dollar contracts at home and spreads abroad

title: Bank of England launches policy statement and draft rules on regulating systemic stablecoins
date_evidence: visible on page: "Published on 22 June 2026" ; notes to editors: "Sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins" 22 June 2026
key_claim: The Bank published its policy statement and draft Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers, raising the maximum share of backing assets held in short-term UK government debt from 60 per cent to 70 per cent and replacing proposed holding limits with a temporary issuance guardrail initially set at 40 billion pounds; feedback closes 22 September 2026 and the Code is to be finalised by end-2026.
frame_summary: Argues that a supervised sterling stablecoin regime with prompt redemption and central bank support is what makes a new form of private digital money trustworthy enough to scale in the UK.

title: Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Customer Identification Program
key_claim: FinCEN, the OCC, the Federal Reserve Board, the FDIC and the NCUA jointly proposed a rule treating permitted payment stablecoin issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act and requiring an effective customer identification program, with comments due by 21 August 2026.
frame_summary: Argues that stablecoin issuers should be supervised as regulated financial institutions inside the existing anti-money-laundering perimeter rather than as a separate technology sector.

title: GENIUS Act: Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
key_claim: The OCC proposed a new information collection requiring permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers to file a weekly confidential report for each stablecoin issued and a quarterly report of condition and income.
frame_summary: Argues that stablecoin supervision needs the same routine prudential reporting machinery as bank supervision, building the surveillance layer before any issuer is licensed.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: The Eurosystem's comprehensive payments strategy
key_claim: The Eurosystem set out a payments strategy spanning wholesale, retail and cross-border payments whose four strategic aims include keeping central bank money as the anchor of the two-tier monetary system and achieving European strategic autonomy, advancing the digital euro alongside the Pontes and Appia wholesale DLT tracks.
frame_summary: Argues that Europe should absorb tokenisation into a system anchored in central bank money and reduce dependence on non-European payment providers and dollar stablecoins.

verbatim_quote: The Financial Stability Board’s thematic peer review on crypto-assets, published in October 2025, revealed that the global regulatory framework and its implementation remain fragmented, with inconsistent and insufficient cross-border cooperation and coordination.

title: Europe's digital euro heads to last stage of negotiations: what Council and Parliament agree on, and where they still clash
key_claim: The Council adopted its digital euro mandate on 19 December 2025 and the European Parliament its position on 9 July 2026; the first political trilogue took place on 13 July 2026, with holding limits, the compensation model and privacy rules still open.
frame_summary: Argues that the co-legislators have settled the digital euro's architecture and that the unresolved fights over holding limits, merchant compensation and privacy are what will decide whether the end-2026 agreement and 2029 issuance timetable hold.

key_claim: The largest US banks are building a shared tokenised deposit network operated by The Clearing House, targeted for launch in the first half of 2027, while platform providers extend similar infrastructure to the wider banking market.
